BLOCKER: AC-3 cannot be met as specified: Go becomes sole writer to PostgreSQL but no in-scope component regenerates the read-only events.jsonl, so legacy readers silently receive stale data (projection "refresh" trigger has no owner in affected_files).
MAJOR: Per-tenant seq uniqueness not stated as a constraint; design only lists index (tenant_id, seq), allowing concurrent appends to race and produce duplicate seq, breaking AC-1's "exactly events seq>cursor" guarantee.

Migration 0024 down path drops the event authority table (destructive, non-reversible without data loss); no verified backup/restore checkpoint is defined before applying/reverting it (checklist item 1).
CL-011 unaddressed: no design evidence or test that the runtime DB role is NOSUPERUSER/NOBYPASSRLS and remains subject to FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY on events/outbox.
Outbox row-count bound (AC-4) has no enforcing owner or cleanup job before BI-PF-1269; an alert alone does not bound rows, so "observable row-count limits" degrade to unbounded growth.
Object-store orphan cleanup is listed as a guardrail but has no owner, test, or acceptance evidence in the declared files, risking unrecoverable garbage and cost growth.
MINOR: `risks` field is "Not specified." despite a cross-item cutover (1266/1267/1269) with a migration and writer swap; risk register should be populated before Gate 1.5.
Failure matrix error codes (EVENT_OUTBOX_UNBOUNDED, projection stale) have no corresponding metric/log contract test in the listed test files.
Rollback text is only "Revert the change"; it does not state recovery from a migration-interrupted state (checklist item 6).
NIT: Traceability maps FR-4→AC-3 while AC-3 is JSONL and FR-3 is cursor; AC/FR numbering in coverage rows should be reconciled to avoid audit confusion.
SUMMARY: The Go-authority direction is sound and language-rule compliant, but AC-3 is not deliverable without an owned projection producer, and AC-1/AC-4 hinge on unstated uniqueness/bound enforcement. Top risks: stale legacy reads after cutover, duplicate per-tenant seq under concurrency, and unbounded outbox/orphan growth.
